questions.prompt: A pricing page says "$30 per 1M image output tokens". What else do you need for a cost per image?

options.text: How many tokens one image uses at your size and quality.
options.explanation: Right. Tokens per image × price per token = cost of one image.

options.text: Nothing. $30 is the price of one image.
options.explanation: $30 is the price of 1 million tokens. One image uses far fewer.

options.text: The length of your prompt only.
options.explanation: Text input adds a little, but the image output tokens set most of the price.

questions.prompt: OpenAI's two GPT Image 2.5 models have the same token rates. Do they cost the same per image?

options.explanation: OpenAI's guide says equal token rates don't mean equal cost per image.

options.text: Not always. The token count can differ by model and quality setting.
options.explanation: Right. Measure the tokens on a small test run.

questions.prompt: OpenAI's and Gemini's Batch API docs describe the same trade. What is it?

options.text: Half the price, but results can take up to about 24 hours.
options.explanation: Right. Both pages give a 50% discount and a 24-hour turnaround.

options.text: Higher image quality for a higher price.
options.explanation: Batch is about price and speed, not quality.

options.text: Free images if you send more than 100.
options.explanation: Neither page offers free images. Batch halves the price.
